Your side projects 60.8 this week and looks well-balanced across the main attacking sources. Arsenal supply three players and Liverpool two, with Haaland and Salah as your primary captain options. The armband sits with Haaland at 8.2, just 0.3 ahead of Salah; he has a meaningful chance of a ceiling fixture but also some downside risk at 8%.

The model suggests Wood to Watkins, netting 5.1 after hits. Watkins projects 9.1 where Wood sits at 4.2, a substantial gain. You have no free transfers left and only £0.5m in the bank, so this trade would require accepting the four-point cost. Whether that margin justifies the hit depends on your horizon and rank position; the arithmetic favours it over the coming weeks.

Your bench is thin—Mykolenko at 3.1 is the only credible cover—but all three main slots carry reasonable projections. The 3-4-3 shape keeps you flexible if events demand a shift.

Your eleven projects 60.8 and looks settled. Haaland at the helm is marginally ahead of Salah, though the gap is slight — if you see reason to back Salah instead, the loss is minimal. Both sit in a strong midfield core anchored by Palmer and Saka, with the Arsenal and Liverpool overlap lending some comfort through concentrated quality rather than spread.

The proposed transfer of Wood to Watkins gains 5.1 net over the horizon and costs you this week, so it's a move that pays later. Watkins is projected significantly higher than Wood; the arithmetic makes sense. You have the bank space and no free transfers remaining, so taking the hit now frees you for flexibility ahead.

Your bench is thin. Mykolenko at 3.1 is your only usable cover if something changes in the eleven before deadline, and even that is modest. Pope and Anderson project very low.

One note: the ranking reflects player quality and fixture strength ahead, not necessarily who starts. Check team news before lock-in, especially with Gabriel, Gvardiol, and Semenyo.

Your team projects 60.8 this week—solid for a Gameweek 8 lineup with three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. The armband on Haaland lifts it to 69.0, a marginal edge over Salah; Haaland carries more upside (25% chance of 10+) but also tail risk (8% chance of 2 or fewer), whereas Salah's projection is tighter. Either is defensible.

The suggested trade—Wood to Watkins—nets 5.1 points over the horizon after a 4-point hit. You'd be paying to shift from Nottingham Forest to Aston Villa in the forward line. The bench is shallow; Mykolenko at 3.1 is your only meaningful cover, so reliability in the eleven matters here.

Your outfield shape is 3-4-3. Three of your midfielders (Salah, Saka, Palmer) sit in the top tier of projection, which concentrates upside but leaves you exposed if any one underperforms. The same logic applies to your two Manchester City assets. Wood's 4.2 is the weak link in your starting eleven and the natural target for upgrade.

You have £0.5m in the bank and no free transfers, so any move costs. The Watkins trade is marginal enough that it hinges on conviction about the swap itself, not the arithmetic.
